display.purpose: Effectively reserved. Empty states and the rare onboarding moment — the app has no hero.

headline.purpose: Pane titles, dialog titles, section headers. Regular weight, not bold.

title.purpose: Card and list headlines. The only chrome role set to medium weight.

body.purpose: Prose, list supporting text, descriptions. Tracking opens up at 0.031em.

label.purpose: Buttons, nav labels, field labels, badges. Tracking widens as size shrinks.

site-display.purpose: Marketing hero and section heads. Source Serif 4 at 600, tracking -0.04em.

site-body.purpose: Marketing prose, capped at 62ch. System sans.

reading.purpose: Long-form document rendering. 18px desktop / 16px mobile, 65ch measure. Off-limits to chrome tokens.

shadows.name: menu-floating
shadows.purpose: Menus and popovers. The floating-layer default.

shadows.name: dialog-floating
shadows.purpose: Dialogs and bottom sheets. Wider and softer than a menu, because a scrim dims everything beneath.

shadows.name: small-floating
shadows.purpose: Snackbars, toasts, FABs — small surfaces lifting off a known background.

shadows.name: mobile-nav
shadows.purpose: Mobile bottom nav. Upward, because the bar is anchored to the bottom edge.

shadows.name: expanded-rail
shadows.purpose: Expanded navigation rail. Directional — mirror to -10px when the rail grows leftward.

shadows.name: glass
shadows.purpose: Backdrop-filter panels. Indigo-tinted so it survives warm themes.

shadows.name: glass-lg
shadows.purpose: Heavy glass panels. Collapsed to none in E-Ink mode.

shadows.name: site-stuck-header
shadows.purpose: Marketing sticky header, only once it sticks. Geometry never animates — only paint.

shadows.name: site-frame
shadows.purpose: Product screenshots and device mockups only. Dark mode adds a 1px white ring at 0.62 alpha.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for state transitions. Also the emphasized curve in this system.

motion.name: ease-linear
motion.purpose: State-layer opacity and indefinite spinners. Opacity only, so it never reads as motion.

motion.name: duration-medium
motion.purpose: Rail expansion, progress width, container morphs.

motion.name: state-hover
motion.purpose: Material state layer: content-color overlay at hover.

motion.name: state-focus
motion.purpose: Material state layer: content-color overlay at keyboard focus.

motion.name: state-press
motion.purpose: Material state layer: content-color overlay at press.

motion.name: nav-indicator
motion.purpose: Nav pill indicator growing from scale 0.35 to full. Transform + opacity only.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All four duration tokens collapse to 0ms under prefers-reduced-motion, data-reduced-motion, or data-animations=off. Consume tokens, never raw durations.

breakpoints.name: phone-max
breakpoints.purpose: App: shortest viewport edge at or below this classifies as phone. src/lib/presentation.ts.

breakpoints.name: desktop-min
breakpoints.purpose: App: desktop vs compact-desktop boundary. The single most important number in the app shell.

breakpoints.name: mobile-css
breakpoints.purpose: App: the CSS-side phone boundary in src/styles/mobile.css.

breakpoints.name: site-sm
breakpoints.purpose: Marketing: hero reflows to one column below 480px; 389px is the narrow floor.

breakpoints.name: site-md
breakpoints.purpose: Marketing: tablet boundary — hero motion and stage layout switch here.

breakpoints.name: site-lg
breakpoints.purpose: Marketing: content bands and pricing layout widen.

zScale.name: tooltip
zScale.purpose: Tooltips — above snackbars, which can overlap triggers.

zScale.name: critical
zScale.purpose: Anchored reader selection toolbar. Must stay above marketing-capture chrome at 9997.

narrative.overview:
Plethora's chrome is a precision instrument that never changes shape. The theme is the weather inside it. A user can move the app from a VS Code grey to deep-ocean bioluminescence to a Windows 95 bevel, and the buttons stay pill-shaped, the target sizes stay 40px, the state layers stay at Material's opacities, and the z-order contract stays intact. That is the whole idea: the identity is infinitely variable and the instrument is not. Material 3 is the grammar; Plethora themes are the voice.

The aesthetic philosophy is dense, tonal, and unshowy. Density is a feature — this is a reading-and-review tool that people keep open for hours, so screens carry real information rather than air. Tonal carries depth, because a five-step surface-container ladder separates a panel from its background more quietly and more reliably than a drop shadow. Unshowy governs expression: nothing in the chrome animates on hover, nothing lifts, nothing glows. The expressive budget is spent in exactly two places — the reading surface, which is a serif at a 65ch measure, and the ambient animated backdrop, which is where a theme gets to be a shader instead of a palette.

Two worlds ship from this repository and deliberately do not share a palette. The app (src/) is the themed Material 3 instrument above. The marketing site (website/) is a paper-and-ink editorial surface — flat, square-cornered, serif-led, with no theming beyond light/dark. Tokens never cross between them.
keyCharacteristics: One grammar, forty-eight voices — the token floor is static, every theme re-derives the roles above it.
Tonal first, shadow reserved — a box-shadow is a claim that a layer floats; if it doesn't, delete it.
Dense by default — scanability outranks expression in an app people live in.
Interaction state is never carried by color alone — always shape plus tone plus glyph.
40px minimum target, always, on every platform.
Motion is token-gated and collapses to instant under prefers-reduced-motion.
Reading content is off-limits to chrome tokens — it has its own stack, its own measure, its own scale.

rules.name: The Token Floor Rule
rules.body: src/index.css's @theme values exist so utilities compile, not so you can hardcode them. Any hex, radius, duration, or z-index in a className or style string literal in application chrome is an eslint error. Suppress a legitimate exception with // md3-allow: <reason> on the line above — brand logos, extract highlight palettes, and injected reader HTML are the sanctioned cases.

rules.name: The Semantic Chrome Rule
rules.body: Application chrome consumes roles; reading content never does. Document rendering, --reading- typography, and reader font settings are a closed system that must not reference chrome tokens in either direction.

rules.name: The Accidental Violet Rule
rules.body: On the marketing site, violet marks the moment — the hero's primary action, a close button, a link — and never the chrome. It is not a button color for everything; if violet is on more than one button in a viewport, it has stopped being an accent and started being a theme. The site's own note calls this out as D6.

rules.name: The One-Platform Rule
rules.body: Desktop and mobile are different instruments, not one instrument at two sizes. Desktop gets the rail, tabs, panes, and keyboard flow. Mobile gets the bottom nav, sheets, and safe areas. Never stretch one onto the other.

rules.name: The Two-Stacks Rule
rules.body: Sans for chrome, serif for content, never both in one surface. Reading meta is the one sanctioned exception — a reader's byline and metadata stay sans (--reading-meta-size, 0.85em) because they are interface, not prose.

rules.name: The Serif Is Not A Setting Rule
rules.body: The reader's stack is fixed in src/styles/reading.css. Reader size, line-height, and alignment are user settings; the family is not a chrome decision and does not follow the theme.

rules.name: The Floating-Layer-Only Rule
rules.body: If an element scrolls with the content, it does not get a box-shadow. If it does not scroll with the content, it gets one. Adding shadow to an in-flow card is the single most common way this system's depth gets destroyed.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: At rest, every surface is flat and separated only by tone. Motion and shadow appear as a response to state — hover, expansion, elevation, focus — and leave again when the state ends.

dos: Do Do consume semantic roles (--color-surface-container-high, --color-primary) and reach for var(--color-X) so the theme layer can move them.
Do Do check src/components/md3/ first and extend an existing variant before writing a new component file.
Do Do add md-state plus a visible focus treatment to anything interactive, and hold a 40px minimum target — 48px on coarse pointers via md-hit-slop.
Do Do separate depth with the surface-container ladder first, and add a shadow only when the layer genuinely floats.
Do Do indicate state with shape, tone, and a glyph — a checkmark, a pill, an icon — so it survives E-Ink mode, high-contrast themes, and color-vision differences.
Do Do respect the z-scale contract: nav < overlay < dialog < menu < snackbar < tooltip < critical (the anchored reader selection toolbar at 9998 must stay above the marketing-capture chrome at 9997).
Do Do consume motion only through --md-duration- and --md-easing-, so reduced motion collapses everything to instant for free.
Do Do keep reading content on its own stack: 65ch measure, --reading- tokens, never a chrome type class.
donts: Don't Don't put a hex, an arbitrary radius, a raw duration, or a z-index number in a className or style literal. It's an eslint error; // md3-allow: is the escape hatch and needs a reason.
Don't Don't shadow an in-flow element. If it scrolls, it has no box-shadow.
Don't Don't lift, translate, or scale a control on hover. Rail items get a tonal state layer and nothing else.
Don't Don't signal state with color alone.
Don't Don't stretch a desktop pattern onto mobile or a mobile pattern onto desktop. Sheets on desktop, hover-lift on a phone — both wrong.
Don't Don't let reading typography consume chrome tokens, in either direction.

Don't Don't write a new color literal into the marketing site, or a chrome token into the site's paper-and-ink world. The two systems do not share a palette; the site rejects glassmorphism, mesh blobs, particle fields, and purple washes outright.
Don't Don't extend the compat shims. ActionButton/actionVariants, common/ThemeSystem.tsx, hand-rolled fixed inset-0 dialogs, and raw peer-checked toggles are all deprecated.
